article_title: “Flagrant violation”: Judge orders return of illegally removed DACA recipient
article_content:
The Trump administration’s well-known illegal deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia and subsequent resistance to his court-ordered return were emblematic of this government’s lawlessness, especially on immigration-related matters.
But Abrego isn’t the only person who’s been illegally removed by Donald Trump’s administration in his second term as president.
The latest example is documented in a court ruling this week that ordered the government to facilitate the return of an immigrant from Mexico who had protections under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program.
Despite Maria de Jesus Estrada Juarez having those protections, she was removed to Mexico last month.
On Monday, U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins ordered the government to get her back to the U.S. within seven days and to afford her all the rights and benefits afforded by her DACA status, which protects noncitizens from detention or removal, regardless of their immigration history.
The Biden-appointed judge wrote that Estrada Juarez was removed in “flagrant violation” of her DACA protections and due process rights.
The government had argued that the court lacked jurisdiction to consider the matter, much less to order her return to the U.S.
But Coggins said the federal appeals court covering California has recognized, in “extreme circumstances,” that courts can exercise jurisdiction over unlawfully removed noncitizens.
